newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria Bradys steady after payment announcement.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Bradys steady after payment announcement.

text.p: Bulgarian Brady prices held steady after the government announced it had transferred a $135.1 million coupon payment due on Tuesday.
A finance ministry official said the money had been paid to Citibank as debt agent for distribution to investors.
By noon, the price for interest arrears bonds (IABs) were quoted at 49-3/4 to 50-3/8 cents in the dollar.
The level is about unchanged from the New York close on Monday but had slumped this morning on rumours that the payment had been delayed.

However, payment of the Brady coupon had been widely expected and traders said prices would remain very volatile until there was a stable government and agreement for a loan from the International Monetary Fund -- neither of which are certainties.

The country's new president has urged the ruling Socialists, who are still baulking at the idea, to agree to opposition demands for an early election so Bulgaria can get on with desparately-needed reforms.
